Exam Date & Time: 28-Jun-2022 (09:00 AM - 12:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SECOND SEMESTER B.TECH. EXAMINATIONS (MIT BANGALORE) - JUNE/JULY 2022  
  SUBJECT : MME_1051 - BASIC MECHANICAL ENGINEERING  
  BASIC MECHANICAL ENGINEERING [MME-1051]  
Marks: 50                                                                                 Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
1A)          Superheated steam at 10 bar is taken out from a boiler and is passed through a supply  
  pipeline to a nearby industry for its use. The industry strictly requires only wet steam  
  with a dryness fraction of 0.8. (i) If the heat loss through the supply pipeline is 500  
  kJ/kg, what is the temperature of superheated steam at the boiler exit? (ii) If the heat loss  
  in the supply pipeline is limited to 30% of latent heat of vaporization, what should be  
  the condition of steam at boiler exit in order to ensure that the steam supplied to the       (5)  
  industry has the required dryness fraction of 0.8? (iii) If the thermal insulation on the  
  supply pipeline is such that the steam does not loose any heat as it passes through the  
  supply pipeline, should the boiler still supply superheated steam? Elaborate your answer.  
  Assume specific heat of superheated steam as 2.25 kJ/kgK.  
  
1B)           Two boilers supply equal quantity of steam to a common pipeline at 15 bar pressure.  
  The steam from boiler-1 is superheated at 250oC while the condition of steam from  
  boiler-2 is unknown. The steam in the common pipeline is wet with a dryness fraction of  
  0.7 at 15 bar. (i) Determine the condition of steam supplied by boiler-2. (ii) If the steam  
  generation rate from boiler-2 is 10 times higher than its fuel supply rate and feed water (5)  
  is supplied at 20oC, what will be the efficiency of boiler-2? Assume specific heat of  
  superheated steam and saturated water as 2.25 kJ/kgK and 4.187 kJ/kgK respectively.  
  The calorific value of fuel supplied to boiler-2 is 22 MJ/kg.  
  
2A)           A belt drive transmits power between two pulleys that are placed 1.8 m apart with a  
  velocity ratio of 0.2. The belt has an angle of contact of 4 radians with the pulley. The  
  diameter of the larger pulley is 1 m and the driver pulley rotates at 1400 rpm. The initial (4)  
  tension in the belt is 0.8 kN and coefficient of friction is 0.28. Determine the power  
  transmitted by the belt drive. Also find the length of the belt.  
  
2B)           A compound gear train consists of six gear wheels A, B, C, D, E & F where A is the  
  driver gear and F is the driven gear. The number of teeth on gear A and F are 90 and 20  
  respectively. Gear B meshes with gear A and is mounted on the same shaft with gear C  
  which has 80 teeth. Gear D meshes with gear C and is mounted on the same shaft with (3)  
  gear E. Gear F meshes with gear E. The velocity ratio from gear A to F is 80. The  
  velocity ratio from A to B is equal to the velocity ratio from C to D and E to F. Show the  
  gearing arrangement and determine the number of teeth for gears B, D and E.  
  
2C)           An engineer wants to transmit power using gear drives in an engineering application and (3)  
  is encountered with the following two constraints:  
  Constraint 1: The axes of the driver and driven shafts are inclined to one another and  
  intersect when produced.  
  Constraint 2: The driving and driven shafts have their axes at right angles and are non-  
  coplanar.  
  Name the best possible gear drive system that the engineer should choose to overcome  
  each constraint separately and explain its characteristics with a neat sketch.

3A)             Which engine will you select if power should be developed in every revolution of  
  engine crankshaft using petrol as fuel? Explain its operation with a neat sketch clearly    (5)  
  showing the piston position in each stroke.  
  
3B)             A single cylinder IC engine generates an output power of 10 kW when operating at 2000  
  rpm. The engine consumes 2 cc/s of petrol and has a compression ratio of 10. The  
  engine is capable of converting 40% of combustion heat energy into power inside the  
  cylinder during power stroke. The volume of the charge inside the cylinder at the end of  
  compression stroke is 0.2 litre. If the engine is designed such that the power is           (5)  
  developed for every two revolutions of crankshaft in a given cycle of operation, (i) what  
  will be the brake torque? (ii) what is the mean effective pressure? (iii) what is the brake  
  specific fuel consumption in kg/kWh? Assume calorific value of fuel as 22000 kJ/kg and  
  specific gravity of fuel as 0.7 and density of water as 1000 kg/m3.  
  
4A)             Two machining operations are to be carried out on a metal rod using a lathe machine. In  
  the first operation, the length of the rod needs to be reduced. In the second operation, a  
  serrated surface should be generated on the rod surface. Name and explain the suitable (4)  
  lathe operations with a neat sketch.  
  
4B)             Elaborate the important lathe specifications with a neat sketch.  
  (3)  
  
4C)             With a neat sketch elaborate the important features of radial drilling machine.  
  (3)  
  
5A)             Explain in detail the importance of machining and shrinkage allowances in casting  
  process?                                                                                    (4)  
  
5B)             The following machining operation needs to be carried out using a drilling machine:  
  (i) Rightsizing of an existing hole.  
  (ii) Threading inside an existing hole                                                      (3)  
  Name the suitable drilling operation for each case and explain its characteristics with a  
  neat sketch.  
  
5C)             Explain with a neat sketch the principle of fusion welding process which makes use of  
  electric arc for heat generation.                                                           (3)  
  
  
-----End-----
